nextSteps: A physical Apple Silicon Mac: per-process Firefox energy, no setup or admin rights. The most precise option.
A Linux PC on bare metal with an Intel or AMD CPU: run `sudo sysctl kernel.perf_event_paranoid=0` once per boot. Measures the whole CPU package, so close other applications.
A Windows 11 PC on a supported Intel, AMD or ARM CPU: CPU package energy, no setup.
Run the CLI on one of these, or register it as a self-hosted runner so issue scans use it (docs/self-hosted-runner.md).

limitations: The sitemap index names 74 sitemaps and 6 were read, so pages listed only in the others could not be picked.

findings.title: 10 elements with animations or transitions

limitations: Families group the 17 pages measured in this scan out of 4729 the sitemap lists. Their figures are medians of those pages and are not extrapolated to pages that were not measured.

Pages are grouped by how they are built (components, landmarks, scripts and stylesheets, template, URL pattern), not by what they cost. Pages in one family can still differ in content, media and behaviour after interaction.

warnings: No power counters were found in the Gecko profile. Energy values are unavailable on this platform; timing and network metrics are still valid.
Crawl mode is for discovery and broad assessment. It is not a controlled regression workload; use journey mode for A/B comparisons.

Components are recognised from the markup. No figure here is a component’s energy: Firefox’s power counters cover whole processes. Whether changing a component saves energy is for a measured comparison (compare), run with and without the change.

Stylesheets, web fonts and CSS background images are not tied to components. Scripts are tied to one only when the element that loads them sits inside it; bundled and global scripts stay unattributed.
Firefox CPU categories are page-level. web-energy diagnose <url> shows them for one representative page.
At most 24 occurrences are recorded per page (the largest, plus smaller ones holding media or animations); counts and sizes cover every occurrence.
Lighthouse did not run, so there is no element or script evidence. Add --lighthouse to a crawl for it.

remediation.title: Render fewer elements
remediation.action: Paginate or virtualise long lists, render menus and other hidden content on demand rather than on every page, and remove wrappers that exist only for styling.
remediation.rationale: Every element is re-examined on style recalculation and layout, so a large subtree costs work on load and on every later change.
remediation.verify: Compare the template with the smaller markup (a paginated or virtualised variant). Measure it with `web-energy experiment --from <result.json> --item <n>` (interleaved, 10 or more runs per side) on a machine that measures energy, or `web-energy compare` between two builds.

remediation.title: Lazy-load images below the first screen
remediation.action: Add loading="lazy" (and decoding="async") to images below the first screen. Never to the LCP image.
remediation.rationale: Images nobody scrolls to are still downloaded and decoded at load: transfer, decode and memory for nothing.
remediation.verify: Compare the page load with and without loading="lazy". Measure it with `web-energy experiment --from <result.json> --item <n>` (interleaved, 10 or more runs per side) on a machine that measures energy, or `web-energy compare` between two builds.
